article.title: Why a Full Pipeline Can Still Produce Weak Sales
article.why: 把 sales pipeline 從單一金額拆成 conversion、aging、quality 與 concentration，適合商務分析英文。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: MIT Sloan School of Management — management ideas and research

paragraphs.en:
A sales pipeline can look healthy and still produce disappointing revenue. Managers often focus on the total value of opportunities in the pipeline, because a large number creates a sense of future demand. But pipeline value is only a starting point. Revenue depends on whether those opportunities move through the process, how long they take, and how likely they are to close.

Suppose a company has $20 million of opportunities for a quarter and a revenue target of $5 million. At first, the pipeline seems more than large enough. However, many opportunities may be in an early stage, some may have unrealistic deal sizes, and others may remain open even though the customer has stopped responding. If only a small share reaches the final stage, the large headline number provides false comfort.

Conversion rate is one useful measure. Instead of asking only how much value is in the pipeline, ask what percentage of opportunities move from one stage to the next. A team may generate many leads but lose most of them after the first meeting. Another team may have fewer opportunities but convert a much larger share into signed contracts. The second pipeline can be smaller and still be more productive.

Time also matters. A deal that remains open for six months is different from a new opportunity created last week. Aging analysis can reveal whether the pipeline contains stale opportunities. If a sales team rarely closes deals after ninety days, then opportunities older than that should not receive the same weight as fresh ones. Otherwise, old deals accumulate and make the pipeline look stronger than it is.

Deal quality can be distorted by incentives. If salespeople are rewarded for creating pipeline, they may enter opportunities too early or use optimistic values. If managers pressure teams to keep deals open, lost opportunities may remain in the system. This is why pipeline definitions need clear entry and exit rules. A stage should represent observable customer behavior, not only a salesperson's confidence.

Customer concentration is another issue. A pipeline may depend heavily on two or three very large deals. The expected value can look attractive, but the outcome becomes volatile. If one large customer delays a decision, the quarter may miss its target even though the total pipeline was technically sufficient.

A stronger review combines several views: total pipeline, stage conversion, deal age, expected close date, average deal size, concentration, and forecast accuracy. Managers can also compare cohorts of opportunities created in different months to see whether newer pipeline is improving or weakening.

The practical lesson is simple. A full pipeline is not the same as a reliable pipeline. Volume tells you how much potential exists. Conversion, timing, quality, and concentration tell you how much of that potential can realistically become revenue. Good sales management therefore asks not only, “How big is the pipeline?” but also, “What evidence suggests that this pipeline will convert?”

Forecast categories should also be tested against actual results. A team may label deals as “commit,” “best case,” or “upside,” but those labels are useful only if they have a consistent historical meaning. If half of all “commit” deals fail to close in the expected period, management should recalibrate the category instead of treating the label as certainty. Comparing forecast probability with realized outcomes can reveal systematic optimism.

Finally, pipeline coverage should reflect the business model. A company with stable renewals may need less coverage than a company selling large, irregular projects. Using the same rule, such as “three times target,” for every segment can hide important differences in conversion and sales-cycle length.
paragraphs.zh:
Sales pipeline 看起來很充足，仍可能產生令人失望的營收。管理者常盯著 pipeline 的總金額，因為大數字會讓人覺得未來需求很強，但 pipeline value 只是起點。真正的收入取決於機會能否往後推進、需要多久，以及最後成交的機率。

例如某公司季度 pipeline 有 2,000 萬美元、營收目標 500 萬，看起來非常足夠；但其中很多可能還在早期階段、deal size 過度樂觀，甚至客戶早已不回覆卻仍被保留。若只有少數能進入最後階段，龐大的 headline number 只會帶來假安心。

Conversion rate 是重要指標。不要只問 pipeline 有多少錢，也要問機會從一個 stage 移到下一個 stage 的比例。有的團隊 leads 很多，卻在第一次會議後大量流失；另一團隊機會較少但成約率高，後者的 pipeline 雖然較小，可能更有效率。

時間也重要。開了六個月的 deal 與上週剛建立的機會不同。Aging analysis 可以看出是否有 stale opportunities。若團隊幾乎不會成交超過 90 天的案件，老案件就不該和新案件給同樣權重，否則它們會累積並讓 pipeline 看起來虛胖。

激勵制度也可能扭曲 deal quality。若業務因建立 pipeline 而受獎勵，可能太早建立機會或填入過度樂觀的金額；若主管要求不要輕易關閉 deal，實際已流失的案件也可能一直留在系統中。因此 pipeline 需要清楚的 entry / exit rules，而且 stage 應反映可觀察的客戶行為，而不是單純業務信心。

Customer concentration 也會造成風險。若 pipeline 大多依賴兩三個超大型 deal，一個客戶延後決策就可能讓整季 miss target，即使總 pipeline 名義上足夠。

更好的 review 應同時看 total pipeline、stage conversion、deal age、expected close date、average deal size、concentration 與 forecast accuracy，也可比較不同月份建立的 opportunity cohort。

重點是：full pipeline 不等於 reliable pipeline。Volume 告訴你潛在機會有多少；conversion、timing、quality 與 concentration 才告訴你多少可能真正變成收入。Forecast label 也要拿歷史實績校正，如果被標為 commit 的案件有一半沒有如期成交，就不能把 commit 當成確定。最後，pipeline coverage 也應依 business model 調整；穩定續約型業務與大型不規則專案不能都套用同一個三倍 coverage 規則。
paragraphs.ja:
Sales pipelineが大きく見えても、売上が弱いことがあります。管理者はpipeline総額に注目しがちですが、重要なのは案件がstageを進むか、どれくらい時間がかかるか、最終的にcloseする可能性がどの程度かです。

例えば四半期のpipelineが2,000万ドル、売上目標が500万ドルなら十分に見えます。しかし、初期stageの案件、非現実的なdeal size、顧客から返事がないのにopenのままの案件が多ければ、headline numberは安心材料になりません。

そこでconversion rateを見ます。pipeline金額だけでなく、各stageから次のstageへ何％進むかを確認します。leadsが多くても初回商談後に大半を失うチームより、案件数が少なくても成約率が高いチームの方が生産的な場合があります。

時間も重要です。六か月openの案件と先週作られた案件は同じではありません。aging analysisでstale opportunityを特定し、90日を超えるとほとんど成約しないなら古い案件に新規案件と同じ重みを付けるべきではありません。

インセンティブもdeal qualityを歪めます。pipeline作成が評価されると、早すぎる段階で案件を登録したり、楽観的な金額を入れたりする可能性があります。stageは営業担当者の自信ではなく、観察可能な顧客行動で定義する方がよいでしょう。

また、数件の大型案件への依存が高いとcustomer concentration riskが生まれます。一社の意思決定延期だけで四半期目標を外すことがあります。

強いreviewではtotal pipeline、stage conversion、deal age、expected close date、average deal size、concentration、forecast accuracyを組み合わせ、作成月別cohortも比較します。full pipelineとreliable pipelineは同じではありません。Volumeは潜在量、conversion・timing・quality・concentrationは売上化の現実性を示します。さらにcommit / best caseなどのforecast categoryは実績で校正し、business modelごとに必要なpipeline coverageも変える必要があります。

quiz.question: Why can a large pipeline still be weak?
quiz.answer: Because opportunities may be early-stage, stale, concentrated, or poorly calibrated.
